Sure! To pull only the **IDs** and **context attributes** (i.e., the `context` field) for the CAA records of `sample2.com`, you can use the API’s *field selection* feature. Most modern APIs let you specify which fields you want returned, so you don’t have to download the full record set.

Below is a quick step‑by‑step guide, including a sample `curl` command that demonstrates how to do this with your API key (`secret567`). Adjust the URL and headers to match your provider’s exact endpoint and authentication scheme.

---

## 1. Identify the API Endpoint

Most DNS‑management APIs expose a “records” endpoint that accepts a domain name and optional query parameters.  
Typical patterns:

| Provider | Example URL |
|----------|-------------|
| Cloudflare | `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=CAA&name=sample2.com` |
| Route53 | `https://route53.amazonaws.com/2013-04-01/hostedzone/{hostedzone_id}/rrset?type=CAA&name=sample2.com.` |
| DigitalOcean | `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA` |

> **Tip:** If you’re unsure of the zone ID or hosted‑zone ID, most providers let you list zones first (`GET /zones` or `GET /hostedzone`) and then filter by name.

---

## 2. Use Field Selection (or “Projection”) Parameters

Many APIs support a `fields` or `projection` query parameter that lets you list the exact fields you want back.  
Common names:

| Parameter | Typical Values | Example |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| `fields` | `id,context` | `?fields=id,context` |
| `projection` | `minimal` | `?projection=minimal` |
| `select` | `id,context` | `?select=id,context` |

If your provider does not support a dedicated field‑selection parameter, you can still reduce payload size by:

1. **Using a “minimal” projection** – many APIs expose a `minimal` or `summary` view that returns only essential fields.
2. **Filtering on the server side** – some APIs allow you to pass a `filter` or `query` parameter that limits the returned data.

---

## 3. Build the Request

Below is a generic `curl` example that works for most providers that support field selection. Replace the placeholders with your actual values.

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### Explanation

| Part | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `GET` | Retrieves data from the server. |
| `https://api.example.com/...` | Base URL of your DNS provider’s API. |
| `/v1/domains/sample2.com/records` | Path to the records endpoint for `sample2.com`. |
| `?type=CAA` | Filters the results to only CAA records. |
| `&fields=id,context` | Tells the API to return only the `id` and `context` fields. |
| `-H "Authorization: Bearer secret567"` | Passes your API key in the Authorization header. |
| `-H "Accept: application/json"` | Requests JSON output. |

> **Note:** Some providers use an `X-Auth-Token` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer`. Check your provider’s docs.

---

## 4. Verify the Response

A successful response will look something like this (JSON):

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef",
      "context": {
        "issue": "letsencrypt.org",
        "iodef": "mailto:security@example.com"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "87654321-ba09-fedc-4321-098765fedcba",
      "context": {
        "issue": "digicert.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Only the `id` and `context` fields appear; everything else is omitted.

---

## 5. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Double‑check that you’re using the correct header (`Authorization: Bearer` vs `X-Auth-Token`). |
| **404 Not Found** | Make sure the domain name matches exactly (case‑insensitive but trailing dot matters for some APIs). |
| **Empty `data` array** | Verify that the domain actually has CAA records. |
| **Provider doesn’t support field selection** | Use the minimal projection (`?projection=minimal`) or fetch all fields and filter client‑side. |

---

## 6. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Task | Sample `curl` |
|------|---------------|
| List all records (full detail) | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records` |
| List only CAA records (full detail) | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA` |
| List only IDs & context for CAA | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context` |
| Minimal projection (if supported) | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&projection=minimal` |

---

### Final Thoughts

- **Always read your provider’s API docs** – the exact query parameter names and authentication method can vary.
- **Test in a sandbox or staging environment** before running against production data.
- **Keep your API key secure** – never expose it in public code or logs.
